title: A5
subtitle: Equal-area cells for geographic data.
intro: Turn longitude and latitude into pentagonal cell IDs for grouping, joining, and geographic rollups. A5 uses equal-area cells at each resolution, with integer IDs and functions for hierarchy, neighborhoods, and geometry conversion.

reference.name: a5_lonlat_to_cell(lon,lat,res)
reference.description: Map longitude, latitude in degrees to a UBIGINT cell ID.

reference.name: a5_cell_to_lonlat(cell)
reference.description: Return the cell center as [longitude, latitude], not the original point.

reference.name: a5_cell_to_parent(cell,res)
reference.description: Find a coarser ancestor for hierarchical rollups.

reference.name: a5_cell_area(res)
reference.description: Return equal cell area in square meters at a resolution.

reference.name: a5_grid_disk(cell,k)
reference.description: Return cells within k edge steps, including the center cell.

reference.name: a5_cell_to_geometry(cell)
reference.description: Produce a native GEOMETRY polygon for mapping.

reference.name: a5_geometry_to_cells(geom,res)
reference.description: Cover geometry; polygons return a compacted covering.

notes.title: Coordinates and identifiers
notes.body: Pass longitude first, latitude second, in degrees. Resolutions run from 0 to 30; larger values mean smaller cells. Preserve IDs as UBIGINT or use a5_u64_to_hex when exporting to systems with limited integer precision.

notes.title: Render at one resolution
notes.body: Coverings from a5_geometry_to_cells, a5_grid_disk, and a5_compact end in a compaction marker that is not a cell. Expand with a5_uncompact(cells) before unnesting or drawing them. A5 1.0 changed cell IDs: convert stored pre-1.0 IDs once with a5_migrate.

examples.title: Encode New York City
examples.caption: Cell 2760559170984869888; area ≈31,669 m².

examples.title: Count observations by cell
examples.sql:
WITH points(lon,lat) AS (VALUES
  (-74.0060,40.7128), (-74.0061,40.7129),
  (-73.9857,40.7484)
)
SELECT a5_lonlat_to_cell(lon,lat,15) AS cell,
       count(*) AS n
FROM points
GROUP BY cell;
examples.caption: Equal-resolution cell IDs are ordinary grouping and join keys.

examples.title: Roll up and draw a cell
examples.sql:
WITH p AS (
  SELECT a5_lonlat_to_cell(
    -74.0060,40.7128,15) AS cell
)
SELECT a5_cell_to_parent(cell,10) AS parent,
       a5_cell_to_geometry(cell) AS polygon
FROM p;
examples.caption: The parent is a hierarchy key; the polygon is native GEOMETRY.

assertions: SELECT CASE WHEN a5_lonlat_to_cell(-74.0060,40.7128,15)=2760559170984869888::UBIGINT AND abs(a5_cell_area(15)-31669.04205949599)<1e-7 THEN true ELSE error('A5 NYC cell or area mismatch') END;

SELECT CASE WHEN a5_get_resolution(a5_cell_to_parent(a5_lonlat_to_cell(-74.0060,40.7128,15),10))=10 AND typeof(a5_cell_to_geometry(a5_lonlat_to_cell(-74.0060,40.7128,15)))='GEOMETRY' THEN true ELSE error('A5 hierarchy or geometry mismatch') END;
SELECT CASE WHEN a5_hex_to_u64(a5_u64_to_hex(a5_lonlat_to_cell(-74.0060,40.7128,15)))=a5_lonlat_to_cell(-74.0060,40.7128,15) THEN true ELSE error('A5 hex roundtrip mismatch') END;
